facts.frequency: when needed, up to 4 times a day
warnings: If you need it more than 3 times a week, tell your GP or asthma nurse.
get_help: If your inhaler does not help and you are struggling to breathe, call 999.

steps.text: This is your blue inhaler. It helps you breathe.
steps.text_en: This is your blue inhaler. It helps you breathe.
steps.picture_prompt: a blue asthma inhaler held in an open hand

steps.text: Use it when you feel wheezy or tight in your chest.
steps.text_en: Use it when you feel wheezy or tight in your chest.
steps.picture_prompt: a person with a hand on their chest, slightly breathless
a hand shaking a blue inhaler, motion lines

steps.text: Breathe out. Then press once and breathe in slowly.
steps.text_en: Breathe out. Then press once and breathe in slowly.
steps.picture_prompt: a person with lips around an inhaler mouthpiece, pressing the canister

steps.text: Hold your breath for 10 seconds. Then do it again.
steps.text_en: Hold your breath for 10 seconds. Then do it again.
steps.picture_prompt: a person holding their breath, a simple clock showing 10 seconds

steps.text: Take 2 puffs. Do not take more than 4 times a day.
steps.text_en: Take 2 puffs. Do not take more than 4 times a day.
steps.picture_prompt: two puffs icon and four small sun/moon icons for a day

steps.text: If it does not help and you cannot breathe, call 999.
steps.text_en: If it does not help and you cannot breathe, call 999.
steps.picture_prompt: a phone showing an emergency call, a worried person
